corpus_metadata.vat_rate_history_note: All test bills use 15% VAT (the rate effective from 1 April 2018 onwards). For bills predating this, the rate would be 14% (1993-04-07 to 2018-03-31) or 10% (1991-09-30 to 1993-04-06).
corpus_metadata.tariff_basis: May 2023 CoCT residential tariffs used as constants across the corpus. Test focus is parser/analyser correctness, not real-world tariff knowledge.

tier1.purpose: Single-bill error detection. Each error bill has ONE injected error embedded among clean bills. Tests detection rate and false-positive rate.

tier2.purpose: Series-level trend error detection. 12-month sequence for one account with compounding tariff errors, recurring duplicate charges, and carryover balance errors. Tests cross-bill analysis.
tier2.narrative: Months 1-3: clean baseline. Months 4-7: water tariff overcharge compounding (+R0.50/kl per month). Months 5-7: duplicate refuse charge in sundries. Month 8: clean. Months 9-12: payments not credited (carryover error).

tier3.purpose: Edge cases. Stacked errors, magnitude scaling, UNKNOWN_TARIFF behaviour, format/parsing edge cases.

execution_order.step1: Run Tier 1 bills through Billdog. Compare detected findings against expected_findings per bill. Iterate until 100% match.
execution_order.step2: Run Tier 2 series through Billdog. Cross-bill analysis must catch trend errors single-bill analysis cannot.
execution_order.step3: Run Tier 3 edge cases. Confirm stacked errors both caught, magnitude scaling works, UNKNOWN_TARIFF surfaces correctly, no false positives on clean edge cases.
execution_order.step4: Once all 3 tiers pass, proceed to real-bill testing (Test 2) using Jason's actual 36 CoCT bills.

scoring.detection_rate_per_error_type: For each error type, measure: did Billdog catch it? Each error bill has exactly the listed findings expected.
scoring.false_positive_rate: For clean bills, Billdog must produce zero findings. Any finding on a clean bill is a false positive.
scoring.recoverable_amount_accuracy: For each detected error, the recoverable amount Billdog produces must match the expected_recoverable in the answer key (within R1.00 tolerance for rounding).
